text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- Even though the main opposition Socialist Party may take part in June elections, the other parties still threaten to boycott the poll unless President Sali Berisha amends the electoral law.
- Paper publishes documents allegedly showing how the Democratic Party faked parliamentary elections last May.
- Prime Minister Bashkim Fino sent a six-point letter to OSCE special envoy Franz Vranitzky, asking for full guarantees from the international community on upcoming elections.
- Tepelene residents, armed to the teeth, turned back President Berisha's escort and threatened to shoot the president with anti-tank shells if he dared visit their town.
- Justice Minister Spartak Ngjela said in an interview parliamentary elections are unlikely to be held in June.
- The local currency lek could depreciate further despite measures by the central bank if the current economic crisis does not end, analyst Zef Preci is quoted as saying.
- Italian ambassador to Albania Paolo Foresti, known as Berisha's Democratic Party supporter, should leave Tirana.
ALBANIA

- Editorial blames foreign intelligence services for bugging a telephone conversation between Democratic Party chairman Tritan Shehu and Italian ambassador Paolo Foresti, published in an Albanian newspaper on Wednesday, saying its aim was to damage Italian-Albanian relations.
- Paper alleges Socialists want the VEFA investment company to collapse in a clear bid to spark fresh protests of thousands of investors and destabilise the country.

- In a protest statement issued to media, the Journalists League asked the government to secure distribution of rightist newspapers which have been prevented from reaching the south by so-called committees of public salvation.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Socialist leader Fatos Nano said: "We will participate in the upcoming elections only if international institutions give us full guarantees."
- Berisha agreed the electoral central commission would be named by the prime minister but refused to amend the distribution of constituencies.
- Berisha is expected to appoint the new head of National Intelligence Service (Shik) later in the day.
- Italian envoy in Tirana Paolo Foresti said a telephone conversation with Democratic Party leader Tritan Shehu published in a local paper has been forged.
- "Big tremor" at the finance ministry after minister Arben Malaj sacked several ministry and bank directors.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Foreign Minister Arjan Starova said the Union for Democracy, an alliance of Berisha's Democratic Party with some small rightist and centrist parties, will win the elections.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- Vlore residents will never allow Berisha to visit their town, the paper says after rumours the president might visit the port town in the next days.
- By refusing to amend the election law, Berisha wants to turn Albania into a new Bosnia.
